procedural_history.originating_court: High Court of Judicature for Rajasthan at Jaipur
procedural_history.impugned_order: Judgment and Order dated 19.10.2023 of the High Court of Judicature for Rajasthan at Jaipur in SBCRLMTBA No.12009 of 2023, rejecting the petitioner's bail application.
procedural_history.high_court_proceedings: A Coordinate Bench of the High Court granted bail to a co-accused. The petitioner then applied for bail, claiming parity. However, the petitioner's bail application was rejected by another Bench, which took exception to the order granting bail to the co-accused, stating that a Supreme Court judgment (Narcotics Control Bureau v. Mohit Aggarwal) was not taken into consideration.
procedural_history.supreme_court_posture: The petitioner approached the Supreme Court by way of a Special Leave Petition (Criminal) No.15585 of 2023, challenging the High Court's order rejecting his bail application. The petitioner's counsel initially argued the case but then sought permission to withdraw the petition, which was granted. The Supreme Court dismissed the petition as withdrawn but made observations regarding the recurrence of situations where High Courts were not following earlier orders of the Supreme Court in dealing with bail applications. The Supreme Court directed its Registry to communicate the order, along with a copy of an earlier order in SLP (Crl.) No.7203 of 2023, to the Registrars of all High Courts for them to place before the Chief Justices of the respective High Courts.

issue.issue_text: Whether bail applications arising out of the same FIR should be listed before the same Judge to avoid conflicting decisions and ensure consistency.

facts: The Supreme Court observed a recurring procedural issue in various High Courts, particularly the High Court of Allahabad.
The issue was that multiple bail applications arising from the same First Information Report (FIR) were being placed before different judges.
This practice led to an "anomalous situation" where some judges would grant bail while others would refuse it, even when the accused applicants had similar attributed roles in the case.
law: The Court referenced its own earlier orders, specifically a three-Judge Bench order from 31.07.2023, which had already established the principle that it is appropriate for all matters related to a single FIR to be listed before the same judge.
application: The Court reasoned that having the same judge hear all bail applications connected to a single FIR is necessary to ensure "consistency in the orders passed."
It expressed concern over the "lethargy" of High Courts in following this established procedure, which was causing conflicting and inconsistent judicial outcomes.

The Court clarified that this procedural rule does not automatically mean all co-accused are entitled to bail on grounds of parity, as that depends on the specific facts and circumstances of each individual's case. However, the procedural consistency of having one judge decide is paramount.
reasoning.conclusion: The Supreme Court accepted the proposition and reiterated its previous stance. To ensure compliance, it directed its own Registrar (Judicial) to communicate the order to the Registrars of all High Courts, who were then to place it before their respective Chief Justices for implementation. This was done to enforce the procedure of listing all bail applications from the same FIR before the same judge to avoid conflicting decisions.

cases.principle: To establish the precedent and express concern that all matters pertaining to the same FIR should be listed before the same Judge to ensure consistency in orders and avoid conflicting decisions.

ratio_decidendi.ratio: All matters pertaining to one First Information Report (FIR) are to be listed before the same Judge to ensure consistency in the orders passed.
obiter: The principle of listing matters from the same FIR before the same judge does not mean that co-accused are invariably entitled to parity, as such entitlement is dependent on various relevant facts and factors.

judicial_reasoning.core_finding: The court found it appropriate that all bail applications and other matters pertaining to a single FIR should be listed before the same Judge. This procedural directive is intended to ensure consistency in judicial orders and to prevent the anomalous situation where different judges might issue conflicting decisions, such as granting bail to one co-accused while refusing it for another with a similar role.
why_appellant_lost: The special leave petition was dismissed because the counsel for the petitioner sought permission to withdraw it after arguing for some time.
why_respondent_won: The respondent did not win on the merits of the case; the petition was dismissed as withdrawn by the appellant.
policy_considerations: Placing matters arising out of the same FIR before different Judges leads to an 'anomalous situation' where some judges grant bail and others refuse it, even when the roles attributed to the applicants are almost similar.
Listing all matters pertaining to one FIR before the same Judge is necessary 'so that there is consistency in the orders passed' and to 'avoid conﬂicting decisions'.
